title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Vrsar, Croatia: 2027 Guide
metaDescription: Is there all-inclusive in Vrsar? One resort sits 2 km away in Funtana. Prices vs half-board and apartments, who it suits, and nearby options for 2027.
content:
## Does Vrsar Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Not in the town itself. Vrsar's hotels (Pineta, Belvedere, Petalon, Amarin-type resorts in the Maistra network, and the Plava Laguna hotels nearby) mainly sell bed and breakfast or half-board. The one genuine all-inclusive property marketed under the Vrsar name is **Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort**, at Valkanela 2 in Funtana. The town of Vrsar is around 2 km away, Poreč around 8 km and Rovinj around 30 km. Booking platforms often list it as a Vrsar hotel, so travellers searching "all-inclusive Vrsar" end up here.

The resort is a 3-star property with 228 rooms, renovated in 2022. Check-in is from 15:00 and check-out is until 10:00. It has two restaurants, two bars, a seasonal outdoor pool, a kids' club and free parking. The beach is shingle and rock, and guest ratings run around 8.4–8.8 out of 10.

## What Is Included in All-Inclusive Here

Typical Maistra-style all-inclusive covers:

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner as buffet meals
- Snacks between meals
- Soft drinks, local beer and wine, and selected spirits at set hours
- Use of the pool, sports facilities and kids' club
- Entertainment programme, in season

Usually **not** included: sun loungers on some beaches, premium spirits, à la carte restaurants, spa treatments, excursions and the tourist tax (about €1.50–2.00 per adult per night, charged separately). Confirm drink hours and the beach-towel policy when booking, as they differ between operators and seasons.

## All-Inclusive Prices in Vrsar and Funtana (2027 Estimates)

Prices below are approximate per person per night, based on a double room and current rate levels. Peak means July to August; shoulder means May to June and September.

| Option | Peak (Jul–Aug) | Shoulder (May–Jun, Sep) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive, Funtana resort | €100–250 | €60–110 |
| Half-board, Vrsar 3–4★ hotel | €90–150 | €50–90 |
| Private apartment, room only | €20–50 | €15–30 |
| Apartment plus food and drinks (see below) | €50–85 | €40–60 |

Tour-operator package rates for the Funtana resort start from roughly €100 per person per day, while peak-week direct prices for a double room can exceed €500 per night. A three-night package from Germany with flights has been priced at around €428 per person.

A self-catering stay includes cooking some meals plus a daily restaurant meal and drinks. A pizza or pasta dinner in Vrsar costs about €10–16, a local beer €3.50–5 and a glass of Istrian Malvazija €4–6.

## Who Should Choose All-Inclusive

**Families with children under 8.** Fixed meal times, a kids' club, a pool and no cooking suit parents with toddlers. Children's discounts are usually large, and children under 3 often stay free, so the cost per head drops sharply.

**Short stays of 3–5 nights.** Packing a week of self-catering logistics is not worth it for a long weekend. Early-season stays (May, June and September) give the best value.

**Travellers who want no planning.** Fly in, check in, and everything is on site.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

- **Stays of 7 nights or more in July and August.** The peak all-inclusive price is hard to justify over a week. This is usually not worth the extra cost for adults who will spend days in Rovinj, Poreč or on the Lim Fjord.
- **Couples and light eaters.** Two adults who eat out once a day typically spend about half as much in an apartment.
- **Groups of 4–6 adults.** Apartments in Vrsar share costs per person in a way hotel rooms cannot.
- **Food-focused visitors.** Istria's konobas, truffle dishes and fresh fish are the reason many visit. Buffet food is decent but standard.

My blunt verdict: in peak weeks, the Funtana all-inclusive is poor value for couples, because the room rate climbs steeply while the food and drink on offer is basic buffet. Pick it in June or September, or skip it.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Alternatives

- **Funtana (2 km):** Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort, the closest option.
- **Poreč area (8–12 km):** Hotel Albatros Plava Laguna and Hotel Zorna Plava Laguna sell all-inclusive packages in season. Valamar's Tamaris Resort, Pical Family Hotel and Isabella Island Resort also offer all-inclusive.
- **Rovinj (about 30 km):** Family-oriented Maistra hotels such as Amarin offer all-inclusive formats in season.
- **Rabac (about 60 km):** Valamar Bellevue Resort, an all-inclusive 4-star.

## Local Tips

- Book the Funtana resort early for July and August. Rooms on the lower floors of the pavilions are quieter.
- Vrsar's old town and marina are a short drive from Funtana. In summer, taxis or the local bus are easier than parking in the old town.
- Supermarkets in Vrsar and Funtana close around 21:00–22:00 in high season. Self-caterers can stock up on fresh fish at the market in Poreč.
- Many apartments require a minimum stay of 5–7 nights in July and August, so a short all-inclusive stay is often the only option for a long weekend in peak season.

## Practical Decision Guide

Choose all-inclusive if the group has children under 8 and the stay is under 6 nights. Choose half-board if you want a hotel but plan to eat out at lunch. Choose a private apartment if the stay is a week or more, the group has four or more people, or you prefer to eat in local restaurants.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Vrsar?
faq.answer: Not inside Vrsar town. The closest is Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort in Funtana, about 2 km away, which many booking sites list under Vrsar. Other Vrsar hotels mainly sell bed and breakfast or half-board.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person per night near Vrsar?
faq.answer: Roughly €100–250 per person in July and August, and about €60–110 in May, June and September. Children's discounts can lower the family total considerably.

faq.question: What does all-inclusive include at the Funtana resort?
faq.answer: Three buffet meals, snacks, selected drinks, and use of the pool, sports facilities and kids' club. Spa treatments, excursions, premium drinks and the tourist tax are usually extra.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Vrsar?
faq.answer: No. All-inclusive typically costs about €10–40 more per person per night than half-board, depending on the season. It only pays off if you would otherwise buy many drinks and snacks on site.

faq.question: Is an apartment in Vrsar cheaper than all-inclusive?
faq.answer: Yes, usually by 40–60% for two adults, even after eating out once a day. The gap is widest in July and August.

faq.question: Which nearby town has more all-inclusive choice than Vrsar?
faq.answer: Poreč, about 8 km north. It has several all-inclusive hotels from Plava Laguna and Valamar. Rovinj and Rabac have a few more family-oriented options.

quickAnswer: Vrsar town has no all-inclusive hotel. The only one on its doorstep is Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort in Funtana, about 2 km away and often listed under Vrsar. Expect roughly €100–250 per person per night in peak season and €60–110 in shoulder season. It suits families with small children on short stays.
